facts.t: She fights back to back with Guinevere in the fifth raid in nine days, and counts the raids from the siren on the dormitory roof.
She thinks the Enders go for the strongest, and sees more of them turn toward Guinevere than toward anyone.
Since the fish market she keeps a step nearer Guinevere's back.
She steps into a claw meant for Guinevere's open left side; it tears her left glove and cuts her arm, and she fires her orb into the Ender's bare core.
She has dressed her own cuts since she was small, and hides the bandage under a spare pair of gloves and her sleeve.
She thinks her father came back for her and paid for it, and that this debt she pays herself.
She does fifty forms every morning.
Guinevere hears her laugh for the first time after their drawn match: short and rusty.
She kept Guinevere's own words: "Rules are for keeping safe what matters."
Every morning since the ceremony she has set Guinevere's slipping left bow straight before the run.
Since the summer she has sewn two felt dolls, a pink-haired Guinevere and a black-haired Vexana, to give at the fireworks.
When the training hall stays lit late she phones Guinevere and tells her "Go to bed."
She always shuts doors. On the morning of the watch she runs out with her staff and the pink-haired keychain at her belt.
In the Investigation Room corridor she shoves Guinevere clear of a claw coming out of a door in the wall, and the claw closes on her hand instead.
As the claw drags her toward the dark she thinks it is all right, as long as Guinevere is safe.
She shouts "Stay back!" at Guinevere as the door pulls her in.
She has violet eyes and a small mole by her mouth.
In the void the Ender drags her a long way and then lets go; she thinks it was sent to take her, not to kill her.
As a child she slipped out of the shelter by the wall to find her father, because she was afraid to be alone, and an Ender found her first.
Her father's last words to her were "Stay back," said as he stood between her and the Ender.
Since the shelter she has felt she owed a life; after saving Guinevere she thinks it is paid.
She folds her wings and lets herself fall through the void, until the Emblem of Hope warms at her collar.
In her memory under the tree she pats Guinevere's hair for the first time, still learning how hard.
She fires at the Will of the Planet; the shot vanishes into its face and not one plate moves.
She asks the Will whether this is the only way to protect Guinevere. It does not answer.
One wish has sat under everything she does since her father died: that it had been her instead.
She decides to take the Will's orders, walk among its Enders as one of them, and keep close to its body.
She plans to pour all her aspirant power into the Mother Matrix's open core when it opens its chest to fire, knowing it would end her too.
She thinks she cannot stop it from the Academy's side, but might from the Enders' side.
Offered a door home onto the dead ground, she steps back and returns to the void.
In the void purple-black armor cut like an Ender's shell closes over her clothes, with a purple cloak, horns and star-shaped blades.
She moves the Emblem from her collar to the inside of her right sleeve, against her wrist, and hides it there.
Her hair, black all her life, turns blue-lavender, darkening to magenta at the ends.
The void slows her body: she is rarely hungry and sleeps little, curled beside her folded uniform.
In the hollow she trains: violet wings, the great arrow that comes down from above at her call, charged shots and the black orb.
She pays Selena for Ender plating in places: where wreckage lies, before the crews find it.
She stays away so that the star is the one true thing Guinevere gets from her.
She builds a machine from Ender plates in the hollow, beating their edges with a hammer until they catch.
As a child she handed her father tools in a gun pit on the city wall without being told which.
She does not mean to come back down from the Mother Matrix.

ties.t: They are partners and make the rule that partners tell each other first.
She pushes Guinevere clear of the claw and is taken in her place.
Her father died standing between her and an Ender.
She decides to let the Will use her and to take its orders.
She means to strike its open core with all her power.
Selena sells her Ender plating in exchange for places.
She builds, wakes and names them.
She fits its plates and core with her own hands.
Chang'e named the void in her class.
She saw Joe's slide of the Storm Citadel in his lesson on weak spots.
She sleeps in the hollow beside her folded clothes.
Her room in the girls' wing holds her things.
She lived there with her father.
She slept on a cot at the home after her father died.
The Will's mark sits behind her breastbone.

gear.name: Vexana's staff
gear.t: Her staff has an orb that fires bolts; she presses it to an Ender's bare core and fires.

gear.name: practice staff
gear.t: She brings a practice staff to the night match.

gear.name: brass collar
gear.t: A brass collar below the orb, fitted round the cracked grip at the team test; it stays brass when the orb turns black.

gear.name: white gloves
gear.t: She wears white gloves and pulls on a spare pair to hide her bandage.

gear.name: Emblem of Hope
gear.t: Guinevere's gold star at her collar, lit when their powers are in sync; later pinned inside her right sleeve.

gear.name: pink-haired keychain
gear.t: A little pink-haired Guinevere at her belt, carried into the void.

gear.name: Vexana's father's toolbox
gear.t: Her father's old toolbox, which still smells of gun oil.

gear.name: Vexana's father's screwdriver
gear.t: She fitted the brass collar with it at the team test.

gear.name: Vexana's Ender armor
gear.t: Purple-black plate, cloak, horns and turning star blades that close over her in the void.

gear.name: Eternal Guards
gear.t: Four giant machines she builds from Ender plating; they run on her power.

gear.name: the hammer
gear.t: Taken from a dead workshop; she beats plate edges with it.

gear.name: the iron bar
gear.t: Taken from a dead workshop; she scratches a line on it each dawn.

gear.name: Vexana's phone
gear.t: Left on her desk when the alarm went, so she has nothing to call with.

facts.t: She likes the front, and in every raid she and Vexana stand there.
She fights the way she does because she never looks back.
She finds Vexana's hidden wound by catching her wrist in sparring, and is hurt that Vexana again carried something alone, after the library.
She challenges Vexana: "Let's settle this with a match, Vexana."
She fights the night match with her left hand tucked into her belt, one arm each, and never goes for Vexana's hurt left arm.
The match ends in a draw, so they both make the rule: partners tell each other first.
She keeps one thing to herself: the bench outside her father's office and the paper she held up to the gap in his door.
She slips a month's plan under Vexana's door, in three colors of ink as always.
Her left bow always slips by evening.
She plans to watch the fireworks with Vexana at the same place next year.
When Vexana phones to send her to bed, she answers "I'm asleep," which she had not said since the first night.
She decides to name every dead Ender in the Investigation Room.
On the morning run she salutes the courtyard billboard of herself and Vexana: "Morning, legends."
Vexana's push throws her clear of the claw; she hits the floor and rolls over broken glass.
She throws herself at the closing door and misses Vexana's hand by a hand.
For the first time she looks back over her shoulder; she had never needed to before.
Seeing her star still lit, she decides Vexana is still there, just not here.
She punches the white wall until her glove splits and the paint is smeared red.
In her written account she blames herself: she left her back open and Vexana stepped into it.
She goes into Vexana's room for the first time and finds the felt dolls, the card and the white box.
She cries over the white box of things Vexana kept.
She does not take the card, because it is Vexana's to give her next year.
She sleeps with her door open a hand's width, as always.
Her red bows were her mother's; for years no hands but hers had touched them, and then Vexana's.
She trains until her legs give out, counts three herself, and nobody says "Four."
She clips the black-haired keychain to her arm guard so it goes in front of her fist.
She draws a red grid over Terrinia and flies every sector she is cleared for, waiting for her star to beep.
She asks Ruby to make her star into a tracker.
For nights she searches the sky with the observation lab telescope for a door, and writes "Nothing" in the night log.
She soldered every seam of the star herself.
When students mock her, she answers "The great lady Guinevere, if you please."
She asks Lesley for a squad to lead and is refused until she has a lead.
She tries to climb the outer ward's fence at night and is pulled down by a Shield sergeant.
At the counseling section she says only "She's alive" and leaves.
She has written to her father every week since she came to the Academy; his seat stayed empty at the trial and the ceremony.
She refuses her father's order to come home, though it costs her place in the House.
She leaves her lamp burning in her window all night, so that Vexana might see it.
In Vexana's memory she gives Vexana the star on the rooftop, her fingertips wrapped in band-aids where the solder burned her.
When Vexana phoned her late in the hall, she complained that normal people say goodnight.
On Team-Up Day she crossed the courtyard in six strides to ask Vexana to be her partner, and kept asking after Vexana said no.

ties.t: They are partners and both make the rule to tell each other first.
Her father sends word through Hester that she must come home.
Her red bows were her mother's.
Hester tied her bows first and counted the cellar stairs for her when she was a child.
Her place in the House is gone if she does not come home.
She repeats what Teacher Chang'e told them about the Control Core.
Ruby tests her star for her.
She came to the Academy and studies there.
She calls herself and Vexana the best partners in The Aspirants.
She made the stars and soldered every seam herself.
She sleeps in her room in the girls' wing with the door open.

gear.name: Guinevere's drones
gear.t: Two drones that rise at her shoulders when she fights.

gear.name: black gloves
gear.t: She fights up close with her fists in black gloves.

gear.name: Guinevere's arm guards
gear.t: She buckles them on to train; the black-haired keychain hangs from one.

gear.name: Emblem of Hope
gear.t: Her gold star at her collar; it lights only when she and Vexana are in sync.

gear.name: black-haired keychain
gear.t: A little black-haired Vexana from the park.

gear.name: Guinevere's red bows
gear.t: Two red bows in her hair, once her mother's.

gear.name: Guinevere's map
gear.t: A map with a red grid over Terrinia for her search.

facts.t: She is first to reach the corridor after the attack, her long rifle on her back and a squad behind her.
She takes Guinevere by the arm and turns her away from the wall.
She tells Guinevere "There's no time to lament."
She hands Guinevere a notebook and pen to write down everything she saw while she still remembers it.
She reads every line of Guinevere's account and folds the pages into her coat.
She pins the VEXANA: MISSING sheet to the board outside the Combat office and walks away without looking at anyone.
She brings Chang'e a cup of water and a pill, and tells her she has slept eleven hours in six days.
She does not argue with Chang'e; she leans on the door frame with folded arms and waits until Chang'e gives in.
She refuses to let a records clerk mark Vexana Killed in action: "No body, no finding. Her file says Missing. It stays Missing."
She tells Guinevere she will give her a squad when she brings a lead.
She tells Guinevere a lit star is a light, not a lead.
She goes into her office and shuts the door.
In Vexana's memory of the ceremony, Lesley smiled at the two partners.

ties.t: She makes Chang'e take her pill and counts her hours of sleep.
Her squad follows her into the corridor.
She keeps Vexana's file at Missing but will not give Guinevere a squad without a lead.

gear.name: long rifle
gear.t: She carries a long rifle on her back.

gear.name: notebook
gear.t: She carries a notebook and pen in her coat and gives them to Guinevere.

facts.t: She comes in behind Lesley's squad, small among them, and runs a scanner as long as her arm up the white wall.
She says a door that small, inside the dome where Enders already stood, almost never happens, and that it cost them something to open.
When Guinevere asks if the door was aimed, she says she does not know what it was.
She falls asleep at her console in the Science Division, with notes on the void glowing on every screen.
She has a cold and claims colds are optional.
Made to take a pill, she says "I hate scary Big Sis!" and then takes it.
She once told Guinevere's class she would never send a student anywhere she could not bring them back from.
She says she cannot even find the door, and that all her notes amount to nothing.
She sends Guinevere to Ruby, saying Ruby does in four seconds what takes her a week.
She keeps a list on a tablet half her size, with WEEKLY written by hand beside one line.
She calls Ruby's deleted code neat and says it is a shame to delete it.
She tells Mr. Bunny that Angela's doll is a new friend for him.
She named the void in class: the dark behind the world, where the Enders come from.
She taught that to defeat the Will of the Planet they must destroy the Enders' Control Core hidden in its dark void.
She called the Will of the Planet the mind behind the Enders.
She called the Mother Matrix the Will's body, as far as her readings could tell.

ties.t: She calls Lesley scary Big Sis but does what she says.
Mr. Bunny floats at her shoulder.
She taught Guinevere's class.
She taught Vexana's class about the void.
Her lab is in the Science Division.
She sends Guinevere to Ruby for help with the star.

gear.name: scanner
gear.t: A scanner as long as her arm, which she runs up the wall where the door opened.

gear.name: Mr. Bunny
gear.t: Her robot, which floats at her shoulder.

gear.name: tablet
gear.t: A tablet half her size holding her check list.

facts.t: She comes to the Science Division in the morning for Angela's check.
She lays her gloved hand on the bench and green lines run up the screen.
She tells Angela the hidden code lets her stop Angela if Oro ever takes her again, and that if she deletes it, nothing does.
She leaves the choice to Angela: "You're the one who controls yourself. What to do is yours to decide."
She does not say which answer she wants.
When Angela nods, the lock opens under Ruby's hand and the forty lines are deleted.
She tells Angela "Now you're free. Forever."
When Chang'e says deleting the code is a shame, she says "Not really."
She asks Angela what she wants the most.
She reads Guinevere's star by laying her fingertips beside it, sending green lines into the gold.
She finds the star's glow the same at every reading: it does not fade with distance or point a way, it only says yes.
She and Angela keep the tower's sensor array running in the observation lab at night.
She tells Guinevere the lab is closed at night, in her perfect voice.

ties.t: She laughs and Angela smiles back at her, a hand's width away.
Only her hand opens its lock, and she deletes it.
She tests Guinevere's star for her.

facts.t: She sits on the lab bench for her check, with her little doll clipped at her hip.
She looks at the red square for a long time, then nods to have the hidden code deleted.
After the deletion, nothing is left under her walking routines but walking.
Asked what she wants most, she says at once "I want to protect everyone!"
She holds Guinevere's star in both cupped hands, as if it might spill.
Told the star only says yes, she says "Then yes is something."
In the observation lab at night she tells Guinevere she should go.
On the third night she pushes a stool over to the telescope for Guinevere.
At lunch she tells Layla "I came back once. People come back."

ties.t: She smiles back at Ruby.
She keeps the doll clipped at her hip.
Ruby fears Oro might take her again.
She keeps Guinevere company at the telescope.

gear.name: Tetra
gear.t: Her little doll, clipped at her hip.

facts.t: At lunch she sets her tray down across the table from Guinevere.
She tells Guinevere that portals don't give people back.
She tells Guinevere, not unkindly, that the star is a circuit and circuits glitch.

ties.t: Fanny tells her to leave Guinevere be.

facts.t: She tells Layla to leave Guinevere be.

ties.t: She speaks up to Layla at the lunch table.

facts.t: She passes the lab bench with a lollipop in her cheek, Silverbolt clicking at her heel.
Glancing at Guinevere's star, she says to nobody "Lost things turn up."
She is out of the door before anyone can answer.
Every student in Vexana's year knows she sells Ender wreckage at the crews' yard outside the outer fence, after dark.
She sits on a crate at the crews' yard, her Academy jacket open and a salvage pass clipped to its pocket.
When a big man swings at her over a price, she is never where the fists land.
She warns him: "If you get too smug, you'll get tripped up."
She hooks a tarp rope taut with her heel and trips him into the mud.
Seeing Vexana in Ender plate, she only moves her lollipop and says "Nice hair."
Her calm at seeing a classmate in Ender plate nags at Vexana for a moment.
She had said in class that her plating came in any size, for a price.
She says she would take stipend money, but Missing people don't draw a stipend.
She agrees to trade plating for the places of two whole dead Enders.
While sorting plates she tells Vexana that most people think she is dead, but her partner does not.
She sells it as genuine Ender plating and says the last owner didn't complain.
She says goodbye with "Ahaha, bye-bye!"
She charges three places for each core.

ties.t: She sells Vexana Ender plating and cores for places.
Silverbolt clicks at her heel.

ties.with: the big man at the crews' yard
ties.t: She trips him into the mud when he tries to bully her on price.

gear.name: lollipop
gear.t: She always has a lollipop in her cheek.

gear.name: Silverbolt
gear.t: Her machine, which clicks along at her heel.

gear.name: salvage pass
gear.t: Clipped to her jacket pocket at the crews' yard.

gear.name: Academy jacket
gear.t: She wears it open while she trades.

facts.t: She stands at the edge of the Storm Citadel's highest deck as the door closes behind her ship.
The Citadel answers to her and to no one else; she is its Imperatrix, its empress.
The crossing has worn her: her shell has split in fine lines at the wrists and throat, and she means to go down to the body to be healed.
After the storm night she took the Citadel far out into the sea of stars to watch what grew from the seed, thinking her own hand close by would spoil the result.
She waited there year after year and read the pulse every day.
When Enders raid that world she looks out through their eyes, and they never know.
She closed her own end of the line in the moment she first looked at herself.
She tells the empty deck "It's... quiet..."
She has absolute control of everything aboard, and it brings her no satisfaction, only a nothingness that follows her like a shadow.
Years into the watch she felt Enders die with a light burning in their cores; in all her ages no Ender had died like that.
She wants one of the humans' machines that hold that light.
Late in the year before, she sent her pawn her first recall.
She counts everything, but after a while stopped counting the pawn's silences.
She says "Heh... even their defiance is within my predictions."
Her recalls carry nothing of where she is; one day she might send one that does.
She thinks the pawn will not dare follow, and notices with surprise that she would not mind being wrong.
She is amused that the pawn has rules.
She leaves the pawn's thread open, sure it will not lead the pawn to her.
She pays the pawn first in slack, then in places, never in words.
Through dying Enders' eyes she saw young humans in suits destroy an Ender army at a hole in the dome.
When the pulse changes, the body calls its commander in: it calls her.
She tells the holds "The Matrix is transmitting."
She finds it touching that the children of that world wear uniforms and learn to fight her kind.
To her the purge is only the work; what comes after is the question, and the pawn is her way to find out.
She sees one small light burning in the void that is not an Ender's, and knows its kind.
She sends nothing of the light up the line and marks the place; the violet in her eyes brightens.

ties.t: She commands the Citadel; it answers to no one else.
The body made her kind.
The body calls her in as its commander.
She is the commander the body calls in.
One pawn among the humans is hers.

gear.name: Storm Citadel
gear.t: Her ship, the largest of her kind, wrapped in its own violet storm.

facts.t: He floats at Chang'e's shoulder.
When Chang'e coughs in her sleep, a frown comes up on his screen.
He drifts down and stops in front of Angela's doll, close enough to touch its face.

ties.t: He floats at her shoulder wherever she goes.
Chang'e calls Angela's doll a new friend for him.

facts.t: Chang'e taught that to defeat it, the Enders' Control Core hidden in its dark void must be destroyed.
It breaks into Vexana's memory through a tear in the sky: a hand as big as the tree, then an arm and a head.
It is armored in dark violet and crowned with tall spikes and horns, with two violet eyes and a thin streak of light running sideways from one of them.
Its shadow drains the color out of the memory; everything under it goes violet, then black.
Chang'e called it the mind behind the Enders. Nobody had ever seen it.
It has no mouth; its word "Look" comes out of the dark itself.
In the vision, it tells Vexana she has reached the end of her future, that she shall witness life's destruction, and that this is no judgment but the universe's predetermined execution.
Asked if this is the only way to protect Guinevere, it gives no answer and draws back into the dark like a tide.
Vexana reasons that it sends every Ender, knows where they will strike, and has no need to lie to her.
When a door home opens, Vexana thinks it is letting her choose.
Its voice speaks to Vexana inside the cold point in her chest.
Its orders give a place and a time, never a reason.
It sends Vexana only to empty places outside the dome and keeps her from people; she does not know why.

ties.t: Chang'e calls it the mind behind the Enders.
It gives her orders through its mark.
It shows Vexana the vision after saying "Look."
It waits in the dark of the void.

facts.t: In the Will's vision, something vast and winged comes down through a tear in the sky over the Academy's tower.
Chang'e called it the Will's body, as far as her readings could tell.
Vexana plans to be within reach when it opens its chest to fire, and strike its open core.
In the void it lies vast, unlit and unmoving, at the far edge of rows of still Enders.
Vexana thinks the gateway will one day be wide enough for it to pass.
Obsidia sees it as the body that made her kind; it opened the way for her ship.
Obsidia means to go down to it to be healed.
Its signal, the pulse, runs one line down to every Ender and tells them where to go and what to do.
It lies as still as the Citadel's holds.
When it began the gateway, its pulse changed and called its commander in.

ties.t: Chang'e's readings say it is the Will's body.
It made Obsidia's kind.
It is widening the gateway into that world.
It calls Obsidia in as its commander.

facts.t: His toolbox, which Vexana keeps by her desk, still smells of gun oil.
On the day of the shelter by the wall he told Vexana to stay back.
When an Ender found her, he turned back from his gun and planted himself between them.
"Stay back" was the last thing he ever said to her.
He stayed as a soldier carried Vexana away down the street.
He pressed bent brackets straight; Vexana smooths her folded clothes the same slow way.
In the gun pit on the city wall he held out his hand for tools without looking, and Vexana put the right one in it.
He and Vexana lived in the Shield houses in the shadow of the city wall.
On her birthdays he took her up the wall stair, named the bright stars after guns, and gave her one small low star.
A soldier said the Ender never got past him while he stood.
He stood until he fell.

ties.t: He is her father and died protecting her.
He lived in the Shield houses and kept a gun on the city wall.
The toolbox was his.
The screwdriver was his.
He stood between her and the Ender.

facts.t: Guinevere once sat on a bench outside his office and held a paper up to the gap in his door.
He sends word to Guinevere through Hester.
Guinevere wrote to him every week; his only answer came through Hester: a board meeting.
His seat for the House stayed empty at the trial and at the ceremony.
After a Shield sergeant reports Guinevere at a closed fence, he orders her home; if she does not come, her place in the House is gone.
His message holds no word about Guinevere herself.
Hester says he reads the Academy's lists every morning.

ties.t: He is her father.
He can take away Guinevere's place in the House.

facts.t: Guinevere's two red bows were hers.

ties.t: She is Guinevere's mother.
The bows were hers.

facts.t: She waits outside the bars of the Academy gate in her gray coat, the long car behind her with its back door open.
She calls Guinevere "Miss Guinevere" and brings word from her father.
At the trial and the ceremony she sat two rows behind the House's empty seat.
She gives the father's order without softening it: come home, or lose her place in the House.
She inclines her head a single degree, then tells Guinevere low that her father reads the Academy's lists every morning.
She tied Guinevere's bows the first time, the morning Guinevere's hair was long enough.
Seeing Guinevere's healing knuckles, she tells her "Hands home after every punch, miss."
She once counted the cellar stairs aloud so a child in the dark would not cry.
When Guinevere walks away, Hester stays where she is; no car door shuts and no engine starts.

ties.t: She counted the stairs for Guinevere as a child and tied her bows.
She carries his word to Guinevere.
She sits behind the House's seat at Academy events.

facts.t: In his lesson on weak spots, his last slide was a shaking recording from the Academy's oldest records: a ship of black blades over a city in a red sky.

ties.t: Vexana and Guinevere saw his slide in class.
He teaches at the Academy.

things.name: the records clerk
aliases: a clerk from the records office

facts.t: He stands under the board outside the Combat office with a form in his hand.
He says there has been no trace of Vexana since the corridor, and after this long the form says Killed in action.
When Lesley refuses, he takes his form back and goes.

ties.t: He comes from the records office.

facts.t: He pulls Guinevere down by the collar as she climbs the outer ward's fence at night.
He is gray at the temples with a rifle on his back, and works out who Guinevere is from her pink hair and red bows.
He tells her "No pass, no entry, miss."
When she says she will find Vexana, he tells her to do it with a pass.
He walks her back under the lamp and writes her name in his book.
He reports her at a closed fence, at night.

ties.t: He is a Shield sergeant.

facts.t: In a room with soft chairs and a window full of plants, she pours two cups of tea.
She asks Guinevere to sit down and tell her about Vexana.
Guinevere leaves at once, and the tea stays full on the table.

ties.t: She works in the counseling section.

things.name: the big man at the crews' yard

facts.t: He stands at the trestle table shouting at Selena over a crate of plating: "Half price, or I take it!"
He swings at her twice and misses, the second time hitting the post.
He pins a hand beside her head and grins that she has nowhere left to lean.
He trips on the tarp rope, falls in the mud, and stamps off swearing toward the gate.

ties.t: He tries to force her price with his fists.

things.name: the soldier who carried Vexana off

facts.t: He carried the young Vexana off down the street while her father stayed to fight.

ties.t: He carried her away from the Ender.

things.name: the soldier who brought the toolbox

facts.t: He brought Vexana's father's toolbox to the home, set it by her cot, and said "That Ender never got past him. Not while he stood."

ties.t: He carried the toolbox to Vexana.

facts.t: Obsidia planted the seed on that world after the storm night, then went far away to watch what grew.
The line tells Obsidia where her pawn is, that it lives and whether it obeys, and nothing more.
It did not come back when Obsidia sent her first recall late in the year before, or after any recall since.
Obsidia thinks it has learned the humans' ways, and defiance is one of them.
Days after the first silence it opened a thin thread beside her recall, on a storm night, up through the Ender parts of its own machine.
Its first words up the thread were "Not coming back" and "Let's trade."
It reported the Academy's dull routines, last year's suit specifications, how aspirant power drives a suit, and how strong suits run by kind and rank.
Its reports named no person and told nothing about where people could be killed.
Obsidia paid it first in slack, letting the pull in its cells sink to a murmur for a week.
Then she paid it in places: where an Ender had fallen, set in its head before the humans could drag the wreck away.
It sends reports only on storm nights, when lightning hides the thread from human instruments.
Obsidia means it to show her what comes after the purge.

It crosses the dark with its violet storm turning around it.
